titleEn: X Spaces: Ron DeSantis 2024 campaign launch
titleZh: X Spaces：罗恩·德桑蒂斯2024年竞选活动启动
summaryEn: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis announced his 2024 presidential campaign live on a Twitter Space hosted by Elon Musk and moderated by David Sacks; the launch was repeatedly delayed by technical glitches before proceeding.
summaryZh: 佛罗里达州州长罗恩·德桑蒂斯在一场由埃隆·马斯克发起、大卫·萨克斯主持的 Twitter Space 直播中宣布参加2024年总统竞选；启动活动因技术故障多次推迟，之后才得以进行。

segments.textEn: To.
segments.textZh: 到。

segments.textEn: Yeah, well, let's see. So. Yeah, Governor, there's been a lot of speculation over the last couple of months about your plans. I understand that you may have an announcement to make. We've got I think a record audience assembled here. You know, probably the biggest room that's probably ever been assembled online. What would you like to tell them?
segments.textZh: 是的，好吧，让我们看看。那么。是的，州长，过去几个月里，外界对您的计划有很多猜测。据我了解，您可能有一项声明要发表。我想，我们这里聚集了创纪录的听众。你知道，这可能是网上有史以来聚集人数最多的房间。您想对他们说些什么？

segments.textEn: Well, I am running for President of the United States to lead our great American comeback. Look, we know our country's going in the wrong direction. We see it with our eyes and we feel it in our bones. Our southern borders collapse. Drugs are pouring into the country. Our cities are being hollowed out by spiking crime. The federal government's making it harder for the average family to make ends meet and to attain and maintain a middle class lifestyle.
segments.textZh: 好吧，我正在竞选美国总统，以领导我们伟大的美国复兴。听着，我们知道我们的国家正朝着错误的方向前进。我们亲眼看到这一点，也从骨子里感受到这一点。我们的南部边境崩溃了。毒品正大量涌入这个国家。犯罪率飙升，正在掏空我们的城市。联邦政府正让普通家庭更难维持生计，也更难获得并维持中产阶级的生活方式。

segments.textEn: And our president, well, he lacks vigor, flounders in the face of our nation's challenges, and he takes his cues from the woke mob. I don't think it has to be this way. American decline is not inevitable. It is a choice. And we should choose a new direction, a path that will lead to American revitalization. We must restore sanity to our nation. This means embracing fiscal and economic sanity. Stop pricing hard working Americans out of a good standard of living through inflationary borrow print and spending policies.
segments.textZh: 而我们的总统，嗯，他缺乏活力，面对我们国家的挑战时手足无措，而且他听命于觉醒暴民。我不认为事情非得如此。美国的衰落并非不可避免。它是一种选择。而我们应该选择一个新方向，一条将通往美国复兴的道路。我们必须让理智重回我们的国家。这意味着拥抱财政和经济理性。停止通过通胀性的借款、印钞和支出政策，让辛勤工作的美国人无法维持良好的生活水平。

segments.textEn: And please embrace American energy independence. This also means replacing the woke mind virus with reality facts and enduring principles. Merit must trump identity politics. We must return normalcy to our communities. America is a sovereign country. Our borders must be respected. We cannot have foreigners pouring into our country illegally by the millions. We cannot allow drug cartels to poison our population with fentanyl.
segments.textZh: 并且请拥抱美国能源独立。这也意味着用现实、事实和持久的原则取代觉醒思想病毒。能力必须胜过身份政治。我们必须让常态回归我们的社区。美国是一个主权国家。我们的边境必须得到尊重。我们不能让数以百万计的外国人非法涌入我们的国家。我们不能允许贩毒集团用芬太尼毒害我们的民众。

segments.textEn: Public deserve safe communities. And law and order must be maintained in American cities. We can't have inmates running the asylum. And we must reject attacks on the men and women of law enforcement. We also must reestablish integrity in our institutions. This includes the military. I'm proud to be a Navy veteran, an Iraq veteran, and I revere our services. But when revered institutions like those in our military are more concerned with matters not central to the mission, whether it's global warming or gender, ideology and pronouns, morale declines and recruiting suffers.
segments.textZh: 公众理应拥有安全的社区。美国城市必须维持法律与秩序。我们不能让精神病人管理精神病院。我们还必须拒绝对执法部门男女工作人员的攻击。我们也必须在我们的机构中重建诚信。这包括军队。我为自己是一名海军退伍军人、一名伊拉克战争退伍军人而自豪，我敬重我们的军种。但当像我们军队中那些备受敬重的机构更关心与任务核心无关的事务时，无论是全球变暖，还是性别、意识形态和代词，士气就会下降，征兵也会受到影响。

segments.textEn: And you need to eliminate these distractions. And we need to get focused on the core mission. We also cannot have true constitutional government if the most significant issues are decided by the whims of unelected bureaucrats rather than the people's elected representatives. Reestablishing integrity in our institutions means we must reinvigorate our constitutional system by returning the government to its rightful owners.
segments.textZh: 而你需要消除这些干扰。我们需要专注于核心任务。如果最重大的问题由未经选举的官僚一时兴起决定，而不是由人民选出的代表决定，我们也不可能拥有真正的宪政政府。在我们的机构中重建诚信，意味着我们必须通过把政府归还给其合法所有者，来重振我们的宪政体制。

segments.textEn: We the people, no Social or economic transformation without representation. Truth needs to be our foundation. Common sense can no longer be an uncommon virtue. And in Florida we proved it could be done. We chose facts over fear, education over indoctrination, law and order over rioting and disorder. We held the line when freedom hung in the balance and we're thriving as a result. Florida is the nation's fastest growing state.
segments.textZh: 我们人民，没有代表权，就不能进行社会或经济转型。真相需要成为我们的根基。常识不能再是一种罕见的美德。而在佛罗里达州，我们证明了这是可以做到的。我们选择事实而不是恐惧，教育而不是灌输，法律与秩序而不是骚乱和混乱。当自由命悬一线时，我们守住了防线，因此我们正蓬勃发展。佛罗里达州是全国人口增长最快的州。

segments.textEn: We're number one in net in migration, number one in new business formations, recently ranked number one in education. We have a 50 year low crime rate and one of the lowest tax and debt per capita in America. But we also understand governing is not entertainment. It's not about building a brand or virtue signaling. It is about delivering results. And our results in Florida have been second to none. We can and we must deliver big results for America.
segments.textZh: 我们的净迁入人数排名第1，新企业成立数量排名第1，最近教育也被评为第1。我们的犯罪率处于50年来的最低水平，人均税收和债务也是美国最低之列。但我们也明白，治理不是娱乐。它不是为了打造品牌或进行美德表演。它是为了取得成果。而我们在佛罗里达州取得的成果首屈一指。我们能够、也必须为美国取得重大成果。

segments.textEn: I pledge to be an energetic executive that will take on the important issues. Biden's pursuit inflationary policies that are hurting working people. We will reverse those policies and we'll build an economy where working Americans can achieve a good standard of living. Biden's opened the southern border and allowed massive amounts of drugs to pour into the country. We'll shut down the border, construct a border wall and hold the drug cartels accountable.
segments.textZh: 我承诺成为一名精力充沛、会处理重要问题的行政长官。拜登对正在伤害劳动者的通胀政策的追求。我们将扭转这些政策，并将建设一个让美国劳动者能够达到良好生活水平的经济。拜登开放了南部边境，允许大量毒品涌入这个国家。我们将封锁边境，修建边境墙，并追究贩毒集团的责任。

segments.textEn: Biden's embrace medical authoritarianism such as unconstitutional COVID vaccine mandates. We will ensure that those violations of liberty can never happen again. Biden's allowed WOKE ideology to drive his agenda. We will never surrender to the WOKE mob and we will leave WOKE ideology in the dustbin of history. Biden's also politicized the military and caused recruiting to plummet. We will eliminate ideological agendas from our military.
segments.textZh: 拜登对医疗威权主义的拥抱，例如违宪的 COVID 疫苗强制令。我们将确保这些侵犯自由的行为永远不会再次发生。拜登允许觉醒意识形态主导他的议程。我们绝不会向觉醒暴民投降，我们会把觉醒意识形态丢进历史的垃圾堆。拜登还把军队政治化，导致征兵人数暴跌。我们将从军队中清除意识形态议程。

segments.textEn: Focus the military on the core mission and we will reverse the poor recruiting trends. Finally, Biden's weaponized the power of the administrative state to advance his left wing agenda. We will reconstitutionalize the executive branch and we'll bring the administrative state to heel. Now, you can't do any of that if you don't win. There is no substitute for victory. We must end the culture of losing that has infected the Republican party in recent years.
segments.textZh: 让军队专注于核心任务，我们将扭转糟糕的征兵趋势。最后，拜登把行政国家的权力武器化，以推进他的左翼议程。我们将使行政部门重新符合宪法，并将使行政国家就范。现在，如果你不能获胜，就做不到其中任何一件事。胜利无可替代。我们必须终结近年来侵蚀共和党的失败文化。

segments.textEn: The tired dogmas of the past are inadequate for a vibrant future. We must look forward, not backwards. We need the courage to lead and we must have the strength to win. And to voters who are participating in this primary process, my pledge to you is this. If you nominate me, you can set your clock to January 20, 2025 at high noon. Because on the west side of the US Capitol, I will be taking the oath of Office as the 47th President of the United States.
segments.textZh: 过去陈旧的教条不足以造就充满活力的未来。我们必须向前看，而不是向后看。我们需要领导的勇气，也必须拥有获胜的力量。对于正在参与这场初选的选民，我对你们的承诺是这样的。如果你们提名我，你们可以把时钟设到2025年1月20日正午。因为在美国国会大厦西侧，我将宣誓就任美国第47任总统。

segments.textEn: No excuses. I will get the job done now. These past few years have given me a new appreciation for the fragility of our freedoms. I never thought I would see things in America that we saw during the COVID 19 pandemic. But our founding fathers were keenly aware of the fragility of freedom when they framed our Constitution. They came to arm with having studied the history of every republic in the history of mankind. And they noticed that all of those experiments only had one thing in common, and it was this.
segments.textZh: 不找借口。我现在会把工作做好。过去这几年让我对我们的自由有多么脆弱有了新的认识。我从未想过，我会在美国看到我们在 COVID 19大流行期间看到的那些事情。但我们的开国元勋在制定宪法时，敏锐地意识到了自由的脆弱性。他们带着研究过人类历史上每一个共和国历史的经历来到武装。而且他们注意到，所有这些实验只有一个共同点，那就是这个。

segments.textEn: Every single one of them had failed. And so they knew it fell to our country, the United States of America, to determine whether people could really govern themselves. Could we have a society based on the idea that our rights are God given, not government granted, and that society functions based on the rule of law, not the rule of individual men? And when Dr. Benjamin Franklin walked out of that convention, he was asked, did you deliver a republic or a monarchy?
segments.textZh: 它们无一例外都失败了。因此，他们知道，决定人民是否真的能够自治这一重任落到了我们的国家——美利坚合众国——肩上。我们能否建立一个这样的社会：它基于这样一种理念，即我们的权利由上帝赋予，而非政府授予；社会依据法治而非个别人之治来运转？当本杰明·富兰克林博士走出那场制宪会议时，有人问他：你们带来的是共和国还是君主制？

segments.textEn: He said, a republic, if you can keep it. They knew freedom didn't run on autopilot. They knew each generation would have a responsibility to safeguard freedom. And it's our responsibility to do so at this important juncture in our nation's history. We have a lot of work to do to ensure the country gets back on track. I ask everybody listening to please join me on this mission. Please invest in our campaign by going to rondisantis.com and making a donation.
segments.textZh: 他说，一个共和国，如果你们能守住它的话。他们知道，自由不会靠自动驾驶运行。他们知道，每一代人都有责任捍卫自由。在我国历史的这一重要关头，这样做是我们的责任。为了确保国家重回正轨，我们还有大量工作要做。我请求每一位正在收听的人加入我的这项使命。请访问rondisantis.com并捐款，为我们的竞选活动投入资金。

segments.textEn: Thank you. God bless, and I look forward to the discussion.
segments.textZh: 谢谢。愿上帝保佑，我期待接下来的讨论。

segments.textEn: All right, thank you, Governor. Appreciate that. I guess just as a first follow up here, thank you for putting up with these technical issues. I think we're definitely breaking new ground here. As far as I know, no major presidential candidate has ever announced their, their, their candidacy on social media this way, certainly in a. In a Twitter space. So thank you for doing that. What made you want to kind of take the chance of doing it this way as opposed to just doing it on cable news or the usual way?
segments.textZh: 好的，谢谢您，州长。非常感谢。我想，首先在这里追问一下，感谢您容忍这些技术问题。我认为我们确实正在开辟新天地。据我所知，此前从未有主要总统候选人以这种方式在社交媒体上宣布他们的、他们的、他们的参选，当然更没有在一个。在一个Twitter Space里。因此，谢谢您这么做。是什么让您愿意冒险采用这种方式，而不是直接在有线电视新闻上，或用通常的方式宣布？

segments.textEn: Well, when Covid hit, I had to make decisions about do you go with the crowd, or do you look at the data yourself and cut against the grain? And I chose to do the latter. I faced huge blowback for doing that from the bureaucracy, from elites, from the media. But my view was I had to look out for the people I represented, prefer protecting their jobs over trying to safeguard my own political hide. But it was very, very lonely in a lot of those decisions.
segments.textZh: 好吧，新冠疫情暴发时，我必须作出决定：你是随大流，还是亲自查看数据并反其道而行？我选择了后者。由于这样做，我遭到了来自官僚机构、精英阶层和媒体的强烈反对。但我的看法是，我必须照顾我所代表的人民，宁愿保护他们的工作，也不去设法保住自己的政治饭碗。但在作出其中许多决定时，我非常、非常孤独。

segments.textEn: And part of the reason it was so lonely is because there was a concerted effort to try to stifle Dissent. There was an official narrative about lockdowns, about closing schools, about forced masking, about all these different things that we had to navigate to during COVID And it was an orthodoxy being enforced by the major tech platforms in conjunction with the federal government. And if we can't have an honest debate in a free country about issues that affect hundreds of millions of people, like lockdowns, then what good is the First Amendment at that point?
segments.textZh: 之所以如此孤独，部分原因是有人齐心协力试图压制异议。关于封锁、关闭学校、强制戴口罩，以及我们在新冠疫情期间不得不应对的所有这些不同事情，都有一套官方叙事。这是一套由主要科技平台与联邦政府共同强制推行的正统观念。如果在一个自由国家里，我们不能就封锁这类影响数亿人的问题展开坦诚辩论，那么到那个时候，第一修正案还有什么用？

segments.textEn: Those are precisely the times when we needed to have debate, be robust. You should not be taking down articles that criticize those draconian policies. And yet that's exactly what happened. So it occurred to me that if that had continued, I think free speech in this country was on its way out the door. And so when Elon Musk stepped up to purchase Twitter, he paid a lot of money for it. And I'm sure, because he's a good businessman, Elon, I'm sure you'll end up making money off it, but bottom line is you had to put your money where your mouth is because I think you recognize that you can't have a free society unless we have the freedom to debate the most important issues that are affecting our civilization.
segments.textZh: 那些恰恰是我们需要展开辩论、需要让辩论有力进行的时候。你们不应下架批评那些严苛政策的文章。然而，事实恰恰就是如此。因此我想到，如果这种情况继续下去，我认为这个国家的言论自由就要被扫地出门了。所以，当埃隆·马斯克挺身而出收购Twitter时，他为此花了很多钱。而且我相信，因为他是一位优秀的商人，埃隆，我相信你最终会从中赚到钱，但归根结底，你必须言行一致，真正投入自己的资金，因为我认为你认识到，除非我们拥有就影响我们文明的最重要问题展开辩论的自由，否则我们就不可能拥有一个自由社会。

segments.textEn: That did not happen during COVID The truth was censored repeatedly. And now that Twitter is in the hands of a free speech advocate, that would not be able to happen again on this Twitter platform. So I think what was done with Twitter and is really significant for the future of our country, we cannot have a society in which government is colluding with major tech platforms to enforce an orthodoxy.
segments.textZh: 这在新冠疫情期间并没有发生。真相一再遭到审查。而现在Twitter掌握在一位言论自由倡导者手中，这种事情将无法再在这个Twitter平台上发生。因此，我认为Twitter所经历的事情对我们国家的未来确实意义重大，我们不能拥有一个政府与主要科技平台相互勾结、强制推行一套正统观念的社会。

segments.textEn: Well, thank you. Yeah, we're absolutely committed to freedom of speech and level playing field and just a vigorous debate. And hopefully this can be a platform that brings people of divergent political views to exchange those views, and perhaps some minds will be changed one way or the other.
segments.textZh: 好的，谢谢。是的，我们绝对致力于言论自由、公平的竞争环境以及充满活力的辩论。希望这能成为一个平台，让持不同政治观点的人交流这些观点，或许一些人的想法会以这样或那样的方式发生改变。

segments.textEn: But it's just incredibly important as you highlight that the First Amendment is irrelevant if all the media and the government are operating in lockstep.
segments.textZh: 但正如你所强调的，如果所有媒体和政府都在步调一致地行事，那么第一修正案就毫无意义，这一点极其重要。

segments.textEn: It makes the most important amendment, the one that was most urgently added to the Constitution, moot if you cannot have free and open debate. So Twitter was indeed expensive, but free speech is priceless.
segments.textZh: 如果无法进行自由、公开的辩论，那么最重要的那条修正案，也就是当时最迫切需要加入宪法的那条修正案，就会变得毫无意义。所以 Twitter 的确很昂贵，但言论自由是无价的。

segments.textEn: Awesome. Thank you. So, Governor, I'm going to ask some questions while we get some other kind of speakers in the queue to ask questions. I think maybe some people knew this announcement was coming because there's been no shortage of hip pieces on you in the press over the last week or two. I want to ask you about some of these accusations that are being leveled at you. Last week, the NAACP issued a travel advisory against your state, claiming that Florida is not a safe place for minorities to visit.
segments.textZh: 太棒了。谢谢。那么，州长，在我们安排其他一些发言者进入队列提问时，我要先问几个问题。我想，也许有些人知道这个声明即将发布，因为过去1周或2周里，媒体上关于你的时髦文章并不少。我想问问你对一些针对你的指控有何看法。上周，美国全国有色人种协进会针对你的州发布了一则旅行警告，声称佛罗里达州对少数族裔而言不是一个可以安全到访的地方。

segments.textEn: What do you say to those who've been advised that somehow they aren't welcome in your state?
segments.textZh: 对于那些被告知不知怎么地他们在你的州不受欢迎的人，你有什么话要说？

segments.textEn: Claiming that Florida is unsafe is a total farce. I mean, are you kidding me? You look at cities around this country, they are awash in crime. In Florida, our crime rate is at a 50 year low. If you look at the top 25 cities for crime in America, Florida does not have a single one amongst the top 25. And if you look at cities like Baltimore and Chicago, you got kids more likely to get shot than to receive a first class education.
segments.textZh: 声称佛罗里达州不安全完全是一场闹剧。我的意思是，你在开玩笑吗？看看这个国家各地的城市，它们犯罪泛滥。在佛罗里达州，我们的犯罪率处于50年来的最低水平。如果你看看美国犯罪问题最严重的前25座城市，佛罗里达州没有一座城市位列前25。如果你看看巴尔的摩和芝加哥这样的城市，那里的孩子中枪的可能性比接受一流教育的可能性还高。

segments.textEn: Yet I don't see the NAACP batting an eye about all the outrage and the carnage that's happening in those areas. So this is a political stunt. These left wing groups have been doing it for many, many years. And at the end of the day, what they're doing is colluding with legacy media to try to manufacture a narrative. Now the good news is fewer and fewer Americans are gullible enough to believe this dribble and platforms like Twitter are there where people can debunk these lies in real time.
segments.textZh: 但对于那些地区正在发生的所有暴行和杀戮，我却没看到美国全国有色人种协进会眨一下眼。所以这是一场政治作秀。这些左翼团体已经这样做了很多、很多年。归根结底，他们所做的就是与传统媒体串通，试图炮制一种叙事。好消息是，不加怀疑地相信这种滴流的美国人越来越少，而像 Twitter 这样的平台就在那里，让人们能够实时驳斥这些谎言。

segments.textEn: And I would just say as an American citizen, if you are uncritically accepting narratives spun by legacy media and left wing groups, you're failing at your job of being a conscientious citizen. And I think people just see right through it. And oh, by the way, have any of these travel advisories because they've been doing this for a while. These left wing groups, have any of them worked? Well, we're the number one state for net in migration and have been every year since I've been governor.

So in the same bill that banned critical race theory, we required teaching thoroughly about racial discrimination that occurred in American history. And Florida's history standards require all of those subjects from slavery, reconstruction, segregation, all of that to be taught, and we'll continue to do that.
segments.textZh: 那会制造分裂。那是错误的。我们也不会教人们仇恨自己的国家。但我们会做的是教授准确的历史。所以，在禁止批判性种族理论的同一项法案中，我们要求全面教授美国历史上发生过的种族歧视。佛罗里达州的历史标准要求教授所有这些主题，从奴隶制、重建时期、种族隔离，所有这些内容，我们也将继续这样做。

segments.textEn: So I think what you see is the left and the media colluding on this. They don't want to actually defend what it is that we are actually legislating or regulating. So they create these hoaxes that somehow you don't want kids to learn that slavery existed in America, which is preposterous. No one actually defends the offending material. And the question is, is why are there people intent on trying to get this stuff into the classroom?
segments.textZh: 所以我认为，你所看到的是左翼和媒体在这件事上相互勾结。他们不想真正为我们实际上正在立法或监管的内容辩护。所以他们制造这些骗局，说什么你不希望孩子们了解美国曾存在奴隶制，这简直荒谬。实际上没有人为那些冒犯性材料辩护。而问题是，为什么有人一心想把这些东西弄进课堂？

segments.textEn: And I think it's part of a political agenda. So our mantra in Florida is this purpose of the schools is education, not indoctrination. Yes, I think it's very inappropriate to have sexually explicit material in a fifth grade library, 100%. But it's also the case that if you're focusing on that type of instruction, there's an opportunity cost involved. Why Won't we. Why shouldn't we be doing more on science or reading or math?
segments.textZh: 而且我认为这是政治议程的一部分。所以我们在佛罗里达州的口号是：学校的宗旨是教育，而不是灌输。是的，我认为在五年级的图书馆里放置露骨的色情材料非常不合适，100%。但同样，如果你专注于那类教学，就会涉及机会成本。为什么我们不会。为什么我们不应该在科学、阅读或数学方面做得更多？

segments.textEn: And so I think we're getting it right. And I think almost invariably and Chris Rufos had to deal with this too. When they're trying to craft these narratives, you just peel back the onion. You realize that this is something they're manufacturing.
segments.textZh: 所以我认为我们做对了。而且我认为几乎无一例外，克里斯·鲁福也不得不应对这个问题。当他们试图编造这些说法时，你只要一层层剥开洋葱，就会意识到这是他们制造出来的东西。

segments.textEn: That makes a lot of sense. I mean, I was actually under the impression that there were some books banned. So this is news to me.
segments.textZh: 这很有道理。我的意思是，我其实原以为确实有一些书被禁了。所以这对我来说是个新消息。

segments.textEn: And they actually, there was. The one this week was that Miami Dade county took a book that was about, like, poems from, I think, like Biden's inauguration, and they moved it from elementary school library to middle school library. The media tried to act like somehow this is being banned. And you actually had Miami Dade County Public Schools spokesperson have to come out and say, there's nothing that's been banned or removed.
segments.textZh: 而且他们实际上，曾经有。本周那件事是，迈阿密-戴德县把一本关于，比如，我想是拜登就职典礼上的诗歌之类的书，从小学图书馆移到了初中图书馆。媒体试图表现得好像这本书不知怎么就被禁了。实际上，迈阿密-戴德县公立学校的发言人不得不出面说，没有任何东西被禁或被移除。

segments.textEn: It was basically just determined that this particular book was better suited for middle school. And so they put it in the middle school media center. And the media tries to act like somehow that is offending something with a book ban. So. But I think part of the reason that they're doing that is because, you know, there is actually a movement to ban books from like Amazon and some of these others. California, some municipalities have banned things like To Kill a Mockingbird.
segments.textZh: 基本上只是判定这本特定的书更适合初中。因此他们把它放进了初中的媒体中心。而媒体试图表现得好像这不知怎么就以禁书的方式冒犯了某些东西。所以。但我认为，他们之所以这样做，部分原因是，你知道，实际上确实存在一场要让亚马逊之类的平台禁书的运动。加利福尼亚州的一些市镇已经禁了《杀死一只知更鸟》之类的作品。

segments.textEn: What they're trying to do is see if some of these books pass a WOKE test, and if they don't, they are going against some of those books. Whereas in Florida, you can buy whatever book you want. But that's a different question than what would be appropriate for a third grader or what would be appropriate for a sixth grader. Government, by definition, has to make those choices about what type of curriculum we want to put in front of our students.
segments.textZh: 他们试图做的是，看其中一些书能否通过“觉醒”测试，如果不能，他们就会反对其中一些书。而在佛罗里达，你想买什么书都可以买。但这和什么内容适合3年级学生、什么内容适合6年级学生是不同的问题。按照定义，政府必须就我们希望向学生提供何种课程作出这些选择。

segments.textEn: And the parents obviously have an important voice in that.
segments.textZh: 而家长显然在这方面拥有重要的发言权。

segments.textEn: Absolutely. Well, in fact, a friend of mine, Tim Urban, who has a blog called Wait, Wait, but why? And is really one of the most reasonable people on earth and one of the most recent people I've ever met, had a lot of trouble actually publishing his book simply because it debated sort of sacred cows of WOKE ideology, but probably reasonable book. So that is the kind of de facto book banning and de facto book suppression that I see quite a lot of is that publishers are unwilling to take risks.
segments.textZh: 绝对如此。嗯，事实上，我的一位朋友蒂姆·厄本有一个名为《等等，等等，但为什么？》的博客。他确实是世界上最讲道理的人之一，也是我见过的最新近的人之一。他在出版自己的书时遇到了很多困难，仅仅因为书中辩论了“觉醒”意识形态中某些类似神圣不可侵犯之物的观念，但那可能是一本讲道理的书。所以，我经常看到的正是这种事实上的禁书和事实上的书籍压制，因为出版商不愿承担风险。

segments.textEn: Let me shift gears here for a second because I know we're running out of time. We're supposed to end, I think around four, but for Pacific. But thank you for giving us a little bit extra time here, Governor. Shifting gears to a Major federal issue, immigration. We see kind of, I've seen these videos on social media and on TV of what looks like just insanity at the border. What is your take on what's going on there and how would you address that as president?
segments.textZh: 让我在这里暂时换个话题，因为我知道我们的时间快用完了。我想我们原定大约4点结束，不过是太平洋时间。但州长，感谢您在这里多给了我们一点时间。换到一个重大的联邦议题：移民。我看到了一些，我在社交媒体和电视上看到了这些视频，边境的情况看起来简直疯狂。您如何看待那里正在发生的事情？如果当选总统，您会如何处理？

segments.textEn: I'd reverse what Biden's doing. You need to shut the border down. You should not be entertaining these asylum claims for people crossing illegally. Now, asylum is a legitimate thing, but these are people that when they come, I mean, they're being persecuted. These people come in overwhelmingly are economic migrants that are coming across many other different countries. They should be applying for asylum there if they were truly qualifying for that, but they're not.
segments.textZh: 我会推翻拜登正在做的事情。你需要关闭边境。你不应该受理这些非法越境者的庇护申请。庇护本身当然是正当的事情，但这些人来到这里时，我的意思是，他们正受到迫害。这些来到这里的人绝大多数是经济移民，他们穿越了许多其他不同的国家。如果他们确实符合庇护资格，就应该在那里申请庇护，但他们并不符合。

segments.textEn: They know that if they just show up at the southern border and these are people all over the world that are coming illegally, they know that they will get a sheet of paper saying, okay, come back for a court date in three years and they get released to the interior of our country. It's an absolutely insane system. So we'll stop that. We will move on day one by declaring a national emergency. We will construct a border wall.
segments.textZh: 他们知道，只要出现在南部边境，而这些人是从世界各地非法来到这里的，他们就知道自己会拿到一张纸，上面写着，好吧，3年后回来出庭，然后他们就会获释，进入我国腹地。这是一个绝对疯狂的制度。所以我们会制止这种情况。我们将在上任第1天宣布全国进入紧急状态，从而采取行动。我们将修建边境墙。

segments.textEn: We will make sure we have remain in Mexico and that we're not entertaining those claims in that way. And we really need to hold the Mexican drug cartels accountable because they're facilitating a lot of this migration. They obviously make money off of it. They treat a lot of these people very horribly as they're trafficking them through Mexico and into the United States. And of course the cartels have been responsible for moving massive amounts of fentanyl into this country and that's killing tens of thousands of Americans every year now.
segments.textZh: 我们会确保实施“留在墨西哥”政策，不以那种方式受理这些申请。我们确实需要追究墨西哥贩毒集团的责任，因为他们为大量此类移民活动提供了便利。他们显然从中牟利。他们在将这些人贩运穿过墨西哥并送入美国的过程中，对其中许多人非常残暴。当然，这些贩毒集团还一直负责将大量芬太尼运入这个国家，而这现在每年都会导致数万名美国人死亡。

segments.textEn: And what they're doing is they laced the other types of drugs with the fentanyl. So you may have like a teenage kid doing something they probably shouldn't do, but in prior generations would not have been fatal. And now if it's laced with fentanyl, you know, these kids can overdose and die. And so mothers are losing kids as a result of this fentanyl epidemic. And I just don't think you could allow these criminal organizations to continue poisoning our population.
segments.textZh: 而他们所做的，是在其他类型的毒品中掺入芬太尼。所以，可能会有一个青少年做了某件他们也许不该做的事，但在过去几代人中，那不会致命。而现在，如果其中掺有芬太尼，你知道，这些孩子可能会用药过量并死亡。因此，由于这场芬太尼流行危机，母亲们正在失去孩子。我就是认为，不能允许这些犯罪组织继续毒害我国民众。

segments.textEn: So it'll be a day one issue. We will bring overwhelming amount of resources to deal with it and we are going to stop this insanity once and for all.
segments.textZh: 所以这会是上任第1天就要处理的问题。我们将投入压倒性的大量资源来应对它，而且我们要一劳永逸地制止这种疯狂局面。

segments.textEn: There's I think follow up question on immigration from Steve Dase, who is a national radio personality and I think important commentator in the great state of Iowa. Steve, do you have a, do you have a comment or question? I think you just need to unmute.
segments.textZh: 我想，史蒂夫·戴斯有一个关于移民问题的后续提问。他是一位全国性电台人物，我认为也是伟大的艾奥瓦州一位重要的评论员。史蒂夫，你有，你有什么评论或问题吗？我想你只需要解除静音。

segments.textEn: If Steve can unmute, then we'll go ahead and ask him for a question. If not, we'll. We'll keep rolling here.
segments.textZh: 如果史蒂夫能解除静音，那我们就请他提问。如果不能，我们就。我们继续进行。

segments.textEn: All right, three. Going, going.
segments.textZh: 好了，3。要走了，要走了。

segments.textEn: I'm there, guys. Oh, there you go.
segments.textZh: 我在呢，各位。哦，你来了。

segments.textEn: All right, my bad.
segments.textZh: 好吧，是我的错。

segments.textEn: First of all, I want to echo what Congressman Massie said to Elon. Elon, if I put down money on January 1, 2022, that Twitter was going to be the last bastion of free speech on Earth, brother, I'd be about as rich as you are on that bet right now. I mean, it's incredible what you have done here and the restoration of a lot of accounts of people that were truth tellers and were ran from here for telling the truth. I saw a meme the other day that said, of course, you have scientific consensus when you censor all the scientists who disagree.
segments.textZh: 首先，我想附和马西众议员对埃隆所说的话。埃隆，如果我在2022年1月1日下注，赌 Twitter 会成为地球上言论自由的最后堡垒，兄弟，凭这笔赌注，我现在大概会和你一样富有。我的意思是，你在这里所做的事情令人难以置信，还有恢复了许多人的账号，这些人说出了真相，却因为说真话而被赶出了这里。我前几天看到一个模因，上面写着：当你审查掉所有持不同意见的科学家时，你当然就有了科学共识。

segments.textEn: So I wanted to just say, first and foremost, on behalf of a lot of grateful people around the country and the world, really, thank you very much for that and the investment you made in that cause. Thank you. A question as a follow up to you, Governor, on this very issue with immigration, we have heard a lot over the years, lock her up, drain the swamp. Going to build a beautiful wall. Mexico is going to pay for it. And crowds cheered and everybody loved it.
segments.textZh: 所以我首先想代表全国乃至全世界许多心怀感激的人说，非常感谢你所做的这一切，也感谢你为这项事业作出的投入。谢谢。州长，作为关于移民这个问题的后续，我有一个问题。这些年来，我们听过很多话：把她关起来、抽干沼泽。要建一堵漂亮的墙。墨西哥会为此买单。人群欢呼，每个人都很喜欢。

segments.textEn: And brands got built and nothing got done. What is the bottom line assurance that you can make to the people that are listening right now all over the world and all over the country that you can actually do the agenda that you just articulated when others tweeted about it and talked about it, but then couldn't actually follow through?
segments.textZh: 品牌树立起来了，却什么都没有完成。此刻，世界各地和全国各地的人都在收听，您能向他们作出的最根本保证是什么，让他们相信您确实能够落实刚才阐述的议程，而其他人只是在推文中谈论它、口头上谈论它，最终却无法真正贯彻执行？

segments.textEn: It's a great question because I shared that frustration. I think even my worst critics in Florida will acknowledge when I tell people I'm going to do something, I don't make promises or say I'm going to do something lightly. I thought it through, and I know that I am going to follow through on what I tell people I'm going to do. So this is one, there will be follow through. Number two, I understand the different leverage points that you would have under Article 2 of the Constitution.
segments.textZh: 这是一个很好的问题，因为我也有同样的挫败感。我认为，即使是我在佛罗里达最严厉的批评者也会承认，当我告诉人们我要做某件事时，我不会轻率地作出承诺，也不会轻率地说我要做某件事。我已经深思熟虑，而且我知道，凡是我告诉人们我要做的事，我都会贯彻到底。所以这是第1点，会贯彻到底。第2点，我理解根据宪法第2条所拥有的不同杠杆着力点。

segments.textEn: I study that a lot, becoming governor about Florida's constitution, doing the same thing for the federal constitution. And you've got to know how to use your leverage to advance what you're trying to accomplish. So, for example, you know, there's leverage that we can use vis a vis Mexico that I think presidents have not been. Not been willing to do. I think sometimes for political purposes. But I'll look at, okay, what are all the variety of options we can do?
segments.textZh: 我对此研究了很多，在就任州长时研究佛罗里达州宪法，也对联邦宪法做了同样的事。你必须知道如何运用自己的杠杆，来推进你想实现的目标。所以，比如，你知道，我们可以对墨西哥运用一些杠杆，我认为历任总统一直没有。一直不愿意这么做。我认为有时是出于政治目的。但我会审视，好吧，我们可以采取的所有不同选择是什么？

segments.textEn: Which buttons can I push? And I will do that to be able to bring this issue to a conclusion once and for all. We had Hurricane Ian come through southwest Florida, category four plus storm, September of 2022, and it did a lot of damage. But one of the things it did, it knocked out a bridge going from the mainland to Pine island and it severed the Sanibel Causeway and three, three different locations. And the locals were being told it's going to take six months to get that stuff repaired.
segments.textZh: 我能按下哪些按钮？我会这么做，以便一劳永逸地解决这个问题。2022年9月，4级以上风暴飓风伊恩袭击了佛罗里达州西南部，造成了大量破坏。但它造成的后果之一是摧毁了一座从大陆通往派恩岛的桥梁，并在3个、3个不同位置切断了萨尼贝尔堤道。当地人被告知，修复那些设施需要6个月。

segments.textEn: And so they came to me, even though these were not state owned bridges, and they said, can you help us? And I said, okay, I'll do it. So I got my guys together, I said, listen, no bureaucracy, no red tape and no excuses. Get it done. We need to open these bridges back. Pine Island Bridge reopened three days later. Sanibel Causeway opened two weeks after that, way, way ahead of schedule because we wouldn't take no for an answer.
segments.textZh: 所以他们来找我，尽管这些桥梁并不归州政府所有，他们说，你能帮帮我们吗？我说，好吧，我来做。所以我把手下的人召集起来，我说，听着，不要官僚主义，不要繁文缛节，也不要借口。把事情办妥。我们需要让这些桥梁重新开放。派恩岛大桥在3天后重新开放。萨尼贝尔堤道在那之后2周开放，比计划大大提前，因为我们不接受“不行”这个答案。

segments.textEn: And we wanted to make sure we got it done. So for me, it is not a campaign slogan that you get in and then forget about it. As an American citizen, if I wasn't running, this would be an issue that bothers me. I've put a lot of my capital as Florida governor involved in combating illegal immigration. We banned sanctuary cities my first year. We just did a strong anti illegal immigration bill in Florida. That's one working.
segments.textZh: 而且我们想确保把事情办妥。所以对我来说，这不是一句你上台之后就抛诸脑后的竞选口号。作为一名美国公民，即使我没有参选，这也会是一个让我困扰的问题。作为佛罗里达州州长，我投入了大量政治资本来打击非法移民。上任第一年，我们就禁止了庇护城市。我们刚刚在佛罗里达州通过了一项强有力的反非法移民法案。那是一项正在发挥作用的措施。

segments.textEn: I've put marine assets in the Florida Keys to help the Coast Guard repel boats from places like Haiti. I had people at the southern border right now helping Texas and we've even been able to relocate illegal aliens to places like Martha's Vineyard. So I don't think any governor has probably gone out of his way to do more to try to make an impact on this issue. And I'm not going to take no for an answer. And I think our voters are sick the empty promises.
segments.textZh: 我在佛罗里达礁岛群部署了海上力量，帮助海岸警卫队阻止来自海地等地的船只。我现在派了人员前往南部边境帮助得克萨斯州，我们甚至还成功把非法移民转移到了玛莎葡萄园岛这样的地方。所以我认为，可能没有任何一位州长会如此不遗余力地采取更多行动，试图对这个问题产生影响。而我不会接受“不行”这个答案。我认为我们的选民已经受够了那些空洞的承诺。

segments.textEn: They want to see action.
segments.textZh: 他们希望看到行动。

segments.textEn: Thank you, governor.
segments.textZh: 谢谢您，州长。

segments.textEn: Well, Governor, I saw, yeah, I saw cover of Time magazine this week and I think they were trying to do a negative story because they had. You were sort of scowling in this portrait they made of you. And in the article they call you, they compared you to the Terminator and I think they meant insult. But I thought it was kind of cool. I thought it was a good thing because I think we need a cool headed, ruthless assassin to go in and they take on the woke mob, take on our out of control government and take on problems like the ones at the border.
segments.textZh: 嗯，州长，我看到了，是的，我看到了本周《时代》杂志的封面，我觉得他们是想做一篇负面报道，因为他们弄了。你在他们为你画的这幅肖像里似乎正皱着眉头。文章里他们称你为，他们把你比作终结者，我觉得他们本意是侮辱。但我觉得这还挺酷的。我觉得这是件好事，因为我认为我们需要一个头脑冷静、冷酷无情的杀手进去，而他们去对付觉醒派暴民、对付我们失控的政府，并对付边境之类的问题。

segments.textEn: So again, I thought it made you sound great, even though that may not have been their intention.
segments.textZh: 所以再说一次，我觉得这让你听起来很棒，尽管那可能并不是他们的本意。

segments.textEn: Well, look at the End of the day, this whole business that we're in is about producing results. I don't care about fanfare. You know, I'm the governor, like that is I'm known, right? And I go around the state and everything and people are very nice. And so, I mean, I appreciate the well wishes, but. But I don't need any of the fanfare. I don't need any adulation. I just know I'm in a position where I have a chance to make a difference and I'm either doing it or I'm not.

segments.textZh: 而我们的总统，嗯，他缺乏活力，面对我们国家的挑战时举步维艰。而且他听命于觉醒派暴民。我不认为事情非得如此。美国的衰落并非不可避免。它是一种选择。而我们应该选择一个新方向，一条将引领美国重焕生机的道路。我们必须让理智重回我们的国家。这意味着接受财政和经济上的理智。停止通过会引发通胀的借贷、印钞和支出政策，让勤劳的美国人无力维持良好的生活水平。

segments.textZh: 并且请拥抱美国的能源独立。这也意味着用现实、事实和持久不变的原则取代觉醒思想病毒。才干必须胜过身份政治。我们必须让社区恢复正常。美国是一个主权国家。我们的边境必须得到尊重。我们不能让数以百万计的外国人非法涌入我国。我们也不能允许贩毒集团用芬太尼毒害我们的民众。

segments.textEn: Well, when Covid hit, I had to make decisions about, do you go with the crowd, or do you look at the data yourself and cut against the grain? And I chose to do the latter. segments.textZh: 所以不管怎样，说到这里，我想我应该把话交给。

segments.textEn: Yeah, well, let's see. So, yeah. Governor, there's been a lot of speculation over the last couple of months about your plans. I understand that you may have an announcement to make. We've got, I think a record audience assembled here, you know, probably the biggest room that's probably ever been assembled online. What would you like to tell them?
segments.textZh: 是的，好吧，让我们看看。所以，是的。州长，过去几个月里，外界对你的计划有很多猜测。我了解到你可能有一项声明要发表。我想，我们这里聚集了创纪录的听众，你知道，这可能是有史以来规模最大的线上聊天室。你想对他们说什么？

segments.textEn: Well, I am running for President of the United States to lead our great American comeback. Look, we know our country's going in the wrong direction. We see it with our eyes and we feel it in our bones. Our southern borders collapse. Drugs are pouring into the country. Our cities are being hollowed out by spiking crime. The federal government's making it harder for the average family to make ends meet and to attain and maintain a middle class lifestyle.
segments.textZh: 好吧，我正在竞选美国总统，以领导我们伟大的美国复兴。听着，我们知道我们的国家正朝着错误的方向前进。我们亲眼看到这一点，也切身感受到这一点。我们的南部边境崩溃了。毒品正大量涌入这个国家。激增的犯罪正在掏空我们的城市。联邦政府正让普通家庭更难维持生计，也更难获得并维持中产阶级的生活方式。

segments.textEn: And our president, well, he lacks vigor. Flounders in the face of our nation's challenges and he takes his cues from the woke mob. I don't think it has to be this way. American decline is not inevitable. It is a choice. And we should choose a new direction, a path that will lead to American revitalization. We must restore sanity to our nation. This means Embracing fiscal and economic sanity. Stop pricing hardworking Americans out of a good standard of living through inflationary borrow print and spending policies.
segments.textZh: 而我们的总统，嗯，他缺乏活力。面对我们国家的挑战时举步维艰，而且他听从觉醒派暴民的指示。我不认为事情非得如此。美国的衰落并非不可避免。这是一种选择。而我们应该选择一个新方向，一条将引领美国重焕生机的道路。我们必须让理智重回我们的国家。这意味着拥抱财政和经济理性。停止通过造成通胀的借贷、印钞和支出政策，让勤劳的美国人无力负担良好的生活水平。

segments.textEn: And please embrace American energy independence. This also means replacing the woke mind virus with reality, facts and and enduring principles. Merit must trump identity politics. We must return normalcy to our communities. America is a sovereign country. Our borders must be respected. We cannot have foreigners pouring into our country illegally by the millions. We cannot allow drug cartels to poison our population with fentanyl.
segments.textZh: 并请拥抱美国的能源独立。这也意味着用现实、事实和和持久的原则取代觉醒思想病毒。能力必须胜过身份政治。我们必须让正常状态回归我们的社区。美国是一个主权国家。我们的边境必须得到尊重。我们不能让数以百万计的外国人非法涌入我们的国家。我们不能允许贩毒集团用芬太尼毒害我们的民众。

segments.textEn: Public deserve safe communities. And law and order must be maintained in American cities. We can't have inmates running the asylum. And we must reject attacks on the men and women of law enforcement. We also must reestablish integrity in our institutions. This includes the military. I'm proud to be a Navy veteran, an Iraq veteran, and I revere our services. But when revered institutions like those in our military are more concerned with matters not central to the mission, whether it's global warming or gender, ideology and pronouns, morale declines and recruiting suffers.
segments.textZh: 公众理应拥有安全的社区。美国城市必须维护法律和秩序。我们不能让精神病人管理精神病院。我们还必须拒绝对执法部门男女工作人员的攻击。我们也必须在我们的机构中重新建立诚信。这包括军队。我为自己是一名海军退伍军人、一名伊拉克战争退伍军人而自豪，而且我敬重我们的军种。但当像我们军队中的那些受人敬重的机构更加关心与任务核心无关的事项时，无论是全球变暖，还是性别、意识形态和代词，士气都会下降，征兵也会受到影响。

segments.textEn: And you need to eliminate these distractions. And we need to get focused on the core mission. We also cannot have true constitutional government if the most significant issues are decided by the whims of unelected bureaucrats rather than the people's elected representatives. Reestablishing integrity in our institutions means we must reinvigorate our constitutional system by returning the government to its rightful ownership.
segments.textZh: 而且你需要消除这些干扰。我们需要专注于核心使命。如果最重大的问题是由未经选举的官僚随心所欲地决定，而不是由人民选出的代表决定，我们也不可能拥有真正的宪政政府。重建我们制度的诚信，意味着我们必须通过将政府归还给其正当的所有者，来重振我们的宪政体制。

segments.textEn: We the people. No social or economic transformation without representation. Truth needs to be our foundation. Common sense can no longer be an uncommon virtue. And in Florida we proved it could be done. We chose facts over fear, education over indoctrination, law and order over rioting and disorder. We held the line when freedom hung in the balance. And we're thriving as a result. Florida is the nation's fastest growing state.
segments.textZh: 我们人民。没有代表权，就不得进行社会或经济改造。真相需要成为我们的根基。常识不能再是一种罕见的美德。我们在佛罗里达州证明了这是可以做到的。我们选择事实而非恐惧，选择教育而非灌输，选择法律与秩序而非骚乱与混乱。当自由悬于一线时，我们守住了阵线。因此，我们正蓬勃发展。佛罗里达州是全美人口增长最快的州。

segments.textEn: We're number one in net in migration, number one in new business formations, recently ranked number one in education. We have a 50 year low crime rate and one of the lowest tax and debt per capita in America. But we also understand governing is not entertainment. It's not about building a brand or virtue signaling. It is about delivering results. And our results in Florida have been second to none. We can and we must deliver big results for America.
segments.textZh: 我们在净迁入方面排名第1，在新企业成立数量方面排名第1，最近在教育方面也被评为第1。我们的犯罪率处于50年来的最低水平，人均税负和债务也是全美最低之列。但我们也明白，治理不是娱乐。它不是为了打造品牌或进行道德表态。它关乎交付成果。而我们在佛罗里达州取得的成果首屈一指。我们能够、也必须为美国交付重大成果。

segments.textEn: I pledge to be an energetic executive that will take on the important issues Biden's pursuit inflationary policies that are hurting working people. We will reverse those policies and we'll build an economy where working Americans can achieve a good standard of living. Biden's opened the southern border and allowed massive amounts of drugs to pour into the country. We'll shut down the border, construct a border wall and hold the drug cartels accountable.
segments.textZh: 我承诺成为一名精力充沛的行政长官，处理那些重要问题。拜登推行的通胀性政策正在伤害劳动人民。我们将扭转那些政策，并建立一个让美国劳动者能够达到良好生活水平的经济。拜登打开了南部边境，允许大量毒品涌入这个国家。我们将封锁边境，修建边境墙，并追究贩毒集团的责任。

segments.textEn: Biden's Embrace medical authoritarianism such as unconstitutional COVID vaccine mandates. We will ensure that those violations of liberty can never happen again. Biden's allowed WOKE ideology to drive his agenda. We will never surrender to the WOKE mob and we will leave WOKE ideology in the dustbin of history. Biden's also politicized the military and caused recruiting to plummet. We will eliminate ideological agendas from our military, focus the military on the core mission, and we will reverse the poor recruiting trends.
segments.textZh: 拜登拥抱医疗威权主义，例如违宪的新冠疫苗强制令。我们将确保那些侵犯自由的行为永远不会再次发生。拜登允许觉醒意识形态主导他的议程。我们绝不会向觉醒暴民投降，我们会把觉醒意识形态扔进历史的垃圾堆。拜登还把军队政治化，导致征兵人数暴跌。我们将从军队中清除意识形态议程，让军队专注于核心使命，并扭转糟糕的征兵趋势。

segments.textEn: Finally, Biden's weaponized the power of the administrative state to advance his left wing agenda. We will reconstitutionalize the executive branch and we'll bring the administrative state to heel. Now, you can't do any of that. We if you don't win, there is no substitute for victory. We must end the culture of losing that has infected the Republican Party in recent years. The tired dogmas of the past are inadequate for a vibrant future.
segments.textZh: 最后，拜登把行政国家的权力武器化，以推进他的左翼议程。我们将使行政部门重新符合宪法，并让行政国家俯首听命。现在，你做不了其中任何一件事。我们，如果你赢不了，胜利就无可替代。我们必须终结近年来侵蚀共和党的失败文化。过去那些陈旧的教条不足以支撑一个充满活力的未来。

segments.textEn: We must look forward, not backwards. We need the courage to lead and we must have the strength to win. And to voters who are participating in this primary process, my pledge to you is this. If you nominate me, you can set your clock to January 20, 2025 at high noon. Because on the west side of the US Capitol, I will be taking the oath of Office as the 47th President of the United States. No excuses. I will get the job done now.
segments.textZh: 我们必须向前看，而不是向后看。我们需要领导的勇气，也必须拥有获胜的力量。对于正在参与这场初选的选民，我对你们的承诺是这样的。如果你们提名我，可以把时钟定在2025年1月20日正午。因为我将在美国国会大厦西侧宣誓就任美国第47任总统。没有借口。我现在就会把事情办成。

segments.textEn: These past few years have given me a new appreciation for the fragility of our freedoms. I never thought I would see things in America that we saw during the COVID 19 pandemic. But our Founding Fathers were keenly aware of the fragility of freedom when they framed our Constitution, they came to arm with having studied the history of every republic and the history of mankind. And they noticed that all of those experiments only had one thing in common.
segments.textZh: 过去这几年让我对我们自由的脆弱有了新的认识。我从未想过自己会在美国看到我们在COVID-19疫情期间看到的那些事情。但我们的开国元勋在制定宪法时敏锐地意识到了自由的脆弱，他们在研究了每一个共和国的历史和人类历史之后前来武装。他们注意到，所有这些试验只有一个共同点。

segments.textEn: And it was this. Every single one of them had failed. And so they knew it fell to our country, the United States of America, to determine whether people could really govern themselves. Could we have a society based on the idea that our rights are God given, not government granted, and that society functions based on the rule of law, not the rule of individual men? And when Dr. Benjamin Franklin walked out of that convention, he was asked, did you deliver a republic or a monarchy?
segments.textZh: 那就是这一点。它们无一例外都失败了。因此，他们知道，确定人民是否真的能够自治，这项任务落到了我们的国家、美利坚合众国身上。我们能否拥有一个建立在这种理念之上的社会：我们的权利由上帝赋予，而非政府授予；社会依靠法治而非个别人之治来运转？当本杰明·富兰克林博士走出那场制宪会议时，有人问他：你们带来的是共和国还是君主国？

segments.textEn: He said, a republic if you can keep it. They knew freedom didn't run on autopilot. They knew each generation would have a responsibility to safeguard freedom. And it's our responsibility to do so at this important juncture in our nation's history. We have a lot of work to do to ensure the country gets back on track. I ask everybody listening to please join me on this mission. Please invest in our campaign by going to Ron DeSantis.com and making a donation.
segments.textZh: 他说，一个共和国，如果你们守得住的话。他们知道，自由不会依靠自动驾驶运行。他们知道，每一代人都有责任捍卫自由。在我国历史的这个重要关头，这样做正是我们的责任。为了确保国家重回正轨，我们还有大量工作要做。我请求每一位正在收听的人加入我的这项使命。请访问RonDeSantis.com捐款，为我们的竞选投入资金。

segments.textEn: Thank you. God bless, and I look forward to the discussion.
segments.textZh: 谢谢。愿上帝保佑，我期待接下来的讨论。

segments.textEn: All right, thank you, Governor. Appreciate that. I guess just as a first follow up here, thank you for putting up with these technical issues. I think we're definitely breaking new ground here. As far as I know, no major presidential candidate has ever announced their candidacy on social media this way, certainly in a Twitter space. So thank you for doing that. What made you want to kind of take the chance of doing it this way as opposed to just doing it on cable news or the usual way?
segments.textZh: 好的，谢谢你，州长。非常感谢。我想先在这里追问一下，感谢你容忍这些技术问题。我认为我们无疑正在这里开辟新天地。据我所知，此前没有任何主要总统候选人曾以这种方式在社交媒体上宣布参选，当然也没有在Twitter Space上这么做。所以感谢你这样做。是什么让你愿意冒险采用这种方式，而不是仅仅在有线电视新闻上或以通常的方式宣布？

segments.textEn: Well, when Covid hit, I had to make decisions about, do you go with the crowd, or do you look at the data yourself and cut against the grain? And I chose to do the latter. I faced huge blowback for doing that from the bureaucracy, from elites, from the media. But my view was I had to look out for the people I represented, prefer protecting their jobs over trying to safeguard my own political hide. But it was very, very lonely in a lot of those decisions.
segments.textZh: 嗯，新冠疫情来袭时，我必须作出决定：你是随大流，还是亲自查看数据并逆势而行？我选择了后者。这样做让我遭到了官僚机构、精英和媒体的强烈反对。但我的看法是，我必须照顾好我所代表的人民，宁可保护他们的工作，也不去设法保全自己的政治前途。但在作出其中许多决定时，我都非常、非常孤独。

segments.textEn: And part of the reason it was so lonely is because there was a concerted effort to try to stifle dissent. There was an official narrative about lockdowns, about closing schools, about forced masking, about all these different things that we had to navigate during COVID And it was an orthodoxy being enforced by the major tech platforms in conjunction with the federal government. And if we can't have an honest debate in a free country about issues that affect hundreds of millions of people, like lockdowns, then what good is the First Amendment at that point?
segments.textZh: 之所以如此孤独，部分原因是当时有人齐心协力试图压制异议。关于封锁、关闭学校、强制佩戴口罩，以及我们在新冠疫情期间不得不应对的所有这些不同事情，都存在一种官方叙事。那是一套由主要科技平台与联邦政府联合强制推行的正统观念。如果在一个自由国家里，我们不能就封锁这类影响数亿人的问题展开坦诚辩论，那么到那个时候，第一修正案还有什么用？

segments.textEn: Those are precisely the times when we needed to have debate, be robust. You should not be taking down articles that criticize those draconian policies. And yet that's exactly what happened. So it occurred to me that if that had continued, I think free speech in this country was on its way out the door. And so when Elon Musk stepped up to purchase Twitter, he paid a lot of money for it. And I'm sure because he's a good businessman, Elon, sure, you'll end up making money off it, but bottom line is you had to put your money where your mouth is, because I think you recognize that you can't have a free society unless we have the freedom to debate the most important issues that are affecting our civilization.
segments.textZh: 那些恰恰是我们需要进行辩论、让辩论充分展开的时刻。你们不应该撤下批评那些严酷政策的文章。然而，发生的恰恰就是这种事。所以我想到，如果这种情况继续下去，我认为这个国家的言论自由就要被扫地出门了。因此，当埃隆·马斯克站出来收购Twitter时，他为此付了很多钱。我相信，因为他是一位优秀的商人，埃隆，当然，你最终会从中赚到钱，但归根结底，你必须言行一致、拿出真金白银，因为我认为你认识到，除非我们拥有就影响我们文明的最重要问题展开辩论的自由，否则就不可能拥有一个自由社会。

segments.textEn: That did not happen during COVID The truth was censored repeatedly. And now that Twitter is in the hands of a free speech advocate, that would not be able to happen again on this Twitter platform. So I think what was done with Twitter is really significant for the future of our country. We cannot have a society in which government is colluding with major tech platforms to enforce an orthodoxy.
segments.textZh: 这种情况在新冠疫情期间并不存在。真相一再遭到审查。如今Twitter掌握在一位言论自由倡导者手中，这种情况将无法在Twitter平台上再次发生。因此，我认为Twitter所经历的变化对我们国家的未来确实意义重大。我们不能拥有一个政府与主要科技平台相互勾结、强制推行一种正统观念的社会。

segments.textEn: Well, thank you. Yeah, we're absolutely committed to freedom of speech and level playing field and just a vigorous debate. And hopefully this can be a platform that brings people of divergent political views to exchange those views and perhaps some minds will be changed one way or the other. And. But it's just incredibly important, as you highlight, that the First Amendment is irrelevant if all the media and the government are operating in lockstep.
segments.textZh: 嗯，谢谢。是的，我们绝对致力于言论自由、公平的竞争环境以及充满活力的辩论。希望这能成为一个让政治观点不同的人交流各自观点的平台，也许一些人的想法会以这样或那样的方式发生改变。而且。但是，正如你所强调的，如果所有媒体和政府都步调一致地行动，那么第一修正案就毫无意义，这一点至关重要。

segments.textEn: It makes the most important amendment, the one that was most urgently added to the Constitution, moot if you cannot have free and open debate. So Twitter was indeed expensive, but free speech is priceless.
segments.textZh: 如果不能进行自由、公开的辩论，那么最重要的那条修正案，也就是当时最迫切需要加入宪法的那条修正案，就会变得毫无意义。所以 Twitter 的确很昂贵，但言论自由是无价的。

segments.textEn: Awesome. Thank you. So, Governor, I'm going to ask some questions while we get some other kind of speakers in the queue to ask questions. I think maybe some people knew this announcement was coming because there's been no shortage of hit pieces on you in the press over the last week or two. I want to ask you about some of these accusations that are being leveled at you.
segments.textZh: 太棒了。谢谢。那么，州长，在我们让其他一些发言者进入提问队列的同时，我会问几个问题。我想也许有些人知道这项宣布即将到来，因为过去1周或2周里，媒体上一直不乏攻击你的文章。我想问问你对这些针对你的指控怎么看。
